title: Completeness for flow-preserving rewrite rules
abstract: Complete sets of graphical rewrite rules enable fully graphical reasoning about quantum computations and have been an area of active research for more than a decade. Many recent applications of the ZX-calculus have made use of the close correspondence between ZX-diagrams and computations in the one-way model of measurement-based quantum computation. In this model, various kinds of flow properties ensure deterministic implementability; for ZX-diagrams, these same properties allow efficient translation into quantum circuits (a problem that is known to be #P-hard in general). Therefore, flow-preserving ZX-calculus rewrite rules are of strong interest.   Here, we extend the set of flow-preserving rules appearing in the literature with a few new rules and extensions of existing rules. We then show that the resulting rule set is complete for all flow-preserving translations between ZX-diagrams of appropriate form. The proof employs a manifestly flow-preserving equivalent of circuit extraction, where a diagram with gflow is transformed, using only flow-preserving rewrite rules, into a diagram with causal flow.
summary: This paper develops and proves the completeness of an extended set of flow-preserving rewrite rules within the ZX-calculus. By establishing this completeness, the authors provide a rigorous mathematical foundation to show that certain classes of quantum computations (those admitting efficient circuit extraction) can be fully manipulated using these graphical rules. This is vital for optimizing and verifying measurement-based quantum computation protocols.
main_problem: The central problem is establishing completeness for flow-preserving rewrite rules within the ZX-calculus framework to ensure fully graphical reasoning about quantum computations.
main_result: The authors extend existing flow-preserving rules and prove that the resulting rule set is complete for all flow-preserving translations between appropriate ZX-diagrams.
method: The proof involves a two-stage process: transforming diagrams with Pauli flow into those with causal flow (circuit extraction) using only flow-preserving rules, relying on established circuit rewriting completeness.
model_or_system: The model is quantum computation represented by ZX-diagrams, particularly in the context of measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC). Flow properties (Pauli flow, gflow, causal flow) are key constraints ensuring deterministic implementability.
key_observables: The presence and type of 'flow' (e.g., Pauli flow, gflow, causal flow), which dictates the physical validity and efficient circuit extraction capability of the diagram.
important_parameters: The structure of the graph derived from the computation, including input/output vertices and measurement labels ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The work focuses on restricting to diagrams possessing a defined flow property (like Pauli or causal flow) to enable efficient circuit extraction; general ZX-diagrams are too complex.
figures_summary: Figure 1 details the complete equational theory for the ZX-calculus, while Figure 2 contains the specific set of extended flow-preserving rewrite rules central to the completeness proof.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the ZX-calculus and its connection to MBQC. It then defines various graph-theoretic 'flow' properties (Pauli flow, gflow) for labelled open graphs. The core is proving that an extended set of flow-preserving rewrite rules achieves completeness for these constrained diagrammatic transformations.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous mathematical toolset—a complete rewriting system—to prove the equivalence and implementability of complex quantum circuits derived from abstract graphical models, which is crucial for optimizing quantum algorithms.
